title: Cohort seatbelt strategy and eval tempo for gradual feature experiments
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Objective: Define a robust 'cohort seatbelt' strategy and a tempo-driven evaluation cadence to safely graduate progressive experiments from 0% to full traffic. This ticket formalizes contract thresholds, instrumentation requirements, and the operational handoffs required for canaries, A/B cohorts, and phased feature flags.

Background: Recent rollout incidents showed slow detection of quality regressions when experiments used coarse traffic increments. We need a repeatable pattern that combines small initial cohorts, automated metric gates, rapid rollback paths, and human signoff cadence to reduce time-to-detect while minimizing false alarms. This document focuses on experiment-level contracts (the "seatbelt"), the evaluation tempo (how frequently we analyze and sign off), and the artifacts engineering and ops must deliver.

Proposal summary:
- Cohort design: define named cohorts (pilot-1, pilot-2, ramp-10, ramp-25) with explicit sizing rules, user partitioning seeds, and privacy constraints.
- Seatbelt contracts: per-cohort metric thresholds across latency, error, quality, and cost; each contract includes immediate kill conditions, degraded-mode triggers, and soft-warning thresholds that require PM/Eng review.
- Eval tempo: a 72-hour rapid-observation window for pilot cohorts, followed by daily checks during 7-day ramp stages. Define fixed evaluation points and a maximum allowed decision lag (12h for pilot, 24h for ramp).
- Instrumentation: require feature-flag-level tracing, per-cohort tokenized metrics (p50/p90/p99 latency, completion error rate, hallucination proxy rate, cost-per-1000-requests), and automatic diff dashboards.
- Automation and ops: implement automated metric gates via the Experiments API that can pause or reduce traffic, with a manual 'emergency rollback' button and an auto-throttle when cost or latency anomalies exceed thresholds.

Deliverables:
- PM acceptance criteria and checklist (this ticket).
- Engineering: gating automation (ENG-21781), cohort partitioning library changes (ENG-21782).
- Observability: Grafana dashboard and alert rules (linked above).
- Runbook: a short ops playbook for on-call and incident responders.

Decision rules and thresholds (examples to be calibrated):
- Immediate kill: >3x baseline 5xx rate sustained for 10 minutes OR p99 latency > 3x baseline for 5 minutes.
- Degraded-mode: sustained 2x increase in cost-per-1k over 24h OR quality-proxy delta > 15% versus baseline (requires PM + Eng review).
- Soft warning: 10% relative degradation in a core metric over 24h (alerts PM/owner).

Acceptance criteria: (all must be met before increasing cohort beyond pilot-2)
- Cohort partitioning and sampling code merged and validated in canary environment (ENG-21782 merged).
- Automated gates implemented and unit-tested (ENG-21781) that can reduce traffic programmatically.
- Dashboards show cohort-separated metrics with baseline overlays and annotated thresholds.
- Runbook documented and shared with on-call rotation; at least one tabletop exercise completed.
- Eval cadence schedule published and acknowledged by PM/Eng/On-call.

Monitoring and reporting cadence:
- Pilot cohorts: 0% -> 0.5% -> 1% over a 72-hour observation window with checks at 12h, 24h, and 72h.
- Ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 7-day windows with daily automated gate checks.
- Reporting: daily experiment digest to stakeholders during ramp, weekly summary during extended pilots.

Operational notes:
- Prefer conservative cohort sizes for experiments touching generation quality (text outputs). UI-only or telemetry-only experiments can be more aggressive.
- Ensure pseudo-anonymized cohort labels to avoid PII leakage in dashboards.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments, test the gating automation in staging clusters that mimic customer topology.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: excessive false positives from noisy metrics causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require confirmatory metric or human signoff for non-critical regressions; tune thresholds with bootstrap data.
- Risk: slow human decision-making delaying rollback. Mitigation: implement auto-throttle kill switches for high-confidence signals and train on-call for rapid triage.
- Risk: gaps in instrumentation. Mitigation: block ramps until required metrics are present for the cohort.

Follow-ups after landing:
- Create a lightweight template for experiment proposals that includes the seatbelt contract and tempo schedule.
- Run a cross-functional war game to validate runbook and thresholds.
- Add a post-mortem checklist item to every experiment ticket: confirm seatbelt contract was followed and record any deviations.

Notes on uniqueness: this approach emphasizes a tempo-driven cadence and explicit per-cohort seatbelts (kill/hard-thresholds, soft warnings, and auto-throttle) rather than only static canary sizes. The goal is to balance early detection with low false-positive rate and clear human/automation handoffs.
